segments: The tenth tractate.
"The matters are settled {OCR? / 'We are coming down'},"
and the King of Kings commanded him:
"Go, swear to them."
And they opened the gates of the fortress and came down.
And the King of Kings commanded,
and they were all killed: men, women, sons, daughters, and even infants;
and no one escaped except a single Armenian blacksmith.
And they also killed Fakhr al-Dīn himself, who had sworn to them, along with them,
because Walī al-Dīn bar Ṣafī al-Dīn, the chief of Aleppo, had slandered him,
saying: "He also killed my father and my brothers, for he said to them:
'Surrender the city,
so that you will not die by the sword.'"
And when all these things had reached an end,
the King of Kings left in Palestine a certain chief whose name was Kitbuqa with ten thousand horsemen—
that is to say, a *tūmān*, which is ten thousand—
and he turned back along the way he had come.
And when he reached Tall Bāshir,
news came to him
that the Tatars had captured Mayyāfāriqīn.
And they had also seized al-Malik al-Ashraf, its lord,
and brought him to him,
and there he killed him.
And he set in authority over Mayyāfāriqīn a certain man who was the chief of the stables of the father of al-Ashraf,
whose name was ʿAbdallāh.
Now there occurred in it a severe famine,
the like of which had never been heard of,
until there remained of all the people who were in it
only about one hundred souls;
and with difficulty were they able to subdue it.
One of the notables of Mayyāfāriqīn, who had been rescued from it like a charred brand from the midst of a fiery furnace, recounted to me in the Ordu:
"One day, a craving overcame me to eat a cooked meal of wheat with beef together with my household,
and for five hundred Naṣirī dirhams I was barely able to cook a single pot that was sufficient for us."
And when the King of Kings crossed the Euphrates,
he sent to the lord of Mardin that he should come down to him;
but he refused.
And he also sent al-Malik al-Muẓaffar, his son—
because he, along with the son of Badr al-Dīn, the lord of Mosul, had been in his service against Aleppo—
and said to him:
"Go, warn your father to come down,
and do not let him rebel and perish."
And when he came to his father,
not only did he not listen to him,
but he even bound him and imprisoned him.
And the King of Kings sent forces, and they encamped against Mardin,
and they began to wage war {OCR? fragments from earlier text repeating}
and his name was ʿAbdallāh {OCR? repetition},
